 UNC-Georgia Preview: Tar Heels Welcome First P5 Test After 3-0 Start
 Jack Morris 8h 1 Share Share 
 North Carolina (3-0) vs. Georgia (3-0)
Chapel Hill, N.C. — Dean E. Smith Center
Friday, Nov. 13 at 7 p.m. ET
TV: ESPN2 (Kevin Brown, LaPhonso Ellis)
 Quotables
 “I challenged our manhood at halftime. We had guys that had just played a whole half of basketball with zero rebounds or one defensive rebound. And I went down the whole roster and challenged each player and challenged the group collectively to go out there and stop getting punked. Because the streets talk, and right now the streets are talking.” — Michael Malone after UNC’s win vs. Wyoming
 “We’ve got to be much better than we’ve been in these three (games) to win an ACC game on the road, of course. But we’ve got good players and we’ve got some confident guys. It’s a great practice team.” — Mike White after Georgia’s win vs. Florida Gulf Coast.
 Pregame Notes
 Last Time Out: Five players scored 11 or more points in North Carolina’s 76-63 win over Wyoming Tuesday. Sayon Keita was among that bunch, pairing his career-high scoring with eight rebounds, six blocks and three steals. The Tar Heels separated in the second half after leading by one possession at the break, but despite the win, UNC’s rebounding concerns were on display again. The Cowboys secured 19 offensive boards, including 15 in the first half, and outrebounded Carolina, 43-37.
 Georgia opened the second half against KenPom’s 208th-ranked Florida Gulf Coast with a 24-4 run before ultimately securing an 80-72 victory on Monday. Four Georgia starters scored a team-high 13 points, including three 3-pointers from Blue Cain . The Bulldogs shot 8-for-25 from distance and notched 22 fast-break points.
 Analyzing the Bulldogs: According to Mike White , beginning his fifth season as head coach, Georgia is “behind schedule” three games in. Squaring off with North Carolina Central (350th in KenPom), Presbyterian (264th in KenPom) and FGCU, the Bulldogs’ average margin of victory is 12.7 points. 
 Still, White’s body of work speaks for itself. Since his hiring from Florida in 2022, Georgia has improved in KenPom, NET, KPI, BPI and SOR each consecutive year, although it hasn’t reached the Round of 32 in the NCAA Tournament during his tenure. The Bulldogs went 22-11 (10-8 SEC) last season, earning a No. 8 seed in the big dance, before falling to ninth-seeded Saint Louis, 102-77, in the opening round. 
 That recent trajectory is relevant because White’s 2026-27 squad returns four starters from a year ago, including seniors Cain (13.1 PPG in 2025-26) and Marcus “Smurf” Millender (12.0 PPG in 2025-26), alongside junior Kanon Catchings (11.6 PPG in 2025-26) — who was a transfer portal target of the prior UNC staff — and sophomore Kareem Stagg (4.8 PPG in 2025-26). Another senior, center James Scott , rounds out the projected first team after 27 starts and 3.9 points per game at Ole Miss last season.
 Georgia welcomes key newcomers in addition to its returners, primarily coming off the bench, led by Freddie Dilione (Penn State) and Brady Dunlap (Saint Louis). Dilione, a guard, averaged a team-high 14 points for the Nittany Lions last season, while Dunlap — who had a UNC offer at one point in high school — served a 3-point specialist role with the Billikens and is a 40.2 percent career shooter from beyond the arc. Through three outings, 16 of his 20 attempts this season are from deep, making five of them.
 Despite coming off the bench and playing 9.3 minutes per game, former St. Bonaventure reserve Andrew Osasuyi is Georgia’s second-leading rebounder (5.3 RPG). Freshman guard Donovan Williams Jr. is another name to know off the bench, averaging 13.7 minutes a night. This offseason, On3 named the former three-star prospect one of the 15 most explosive players in the Class of 2026.
 By the Numbers: The Bulldogs’ guards and wings shoulder most of the scoring, but it’s still been a balanced attack of 2-pointers and 3-pointers thus far. At 46 percent from the floor, Georgia hasn’t shot the ball well from deep, firing at 31.2 percent in 25.7 attempts per game — a similar diet shown from North Carolina.
 The perimeter-oriented Bulldogs have received 36 of their 249 points from players 6-foot-10 or taller. That discrepancy hasn’t hindered their rebounding efforts, though. The consensus between KenPom and Bart Torvik is that Georgia is a top-70 offensive rebounding team nationally, with its numbers on the defensive glass around the Division I average.
 The brightest shining layer of the Bulldogs’ resume is their lack of turnovers, tallying a program-record three against Presbyterian last week. Averaging 7.0 per game and an 8.3 margin per game, Georgia ranks fifth nationally in turnover percentage. 
 Cain leads the way with 16.0 points per game and 41.7 percent on 3-point attempts. But Millender, a 5-foot-11, crafty veteran, runs the show at point guard, averaging a team-high 3.7 assists on top of his 12.3 points per game. Catchings is listed as a forward at 6-foot-9, but he spends most of his time on the perimeter, leading the starting lineup in 3-point attempts with 14. 
 Georgia is ranked 49th in Bart Torvik, 52nd in Evan Miya and 65th in KenPom, notably all behind the Tar Heels. The Bulldogs were picked to finish 11th in the SEC preseason poll. 
 The Matchup: Considering the respective strength of schedules, there might be more questions than answers for both teams ahead of the power conference tilt. What’s not in flux, though, is Georgia’s experience and veteran leadership, shown in its ability to take care of the ball. White compared the trip to the Smith Center to an SEC road game, creating intrigue about how his familiar squad will handle its first true test of 2026-27.
 North Carolina bandaged its rebounding struggles enough to avoid a disaster in the opening stretch of the season, but the margin for error regresses with a potential NCAA Tournament team on the other side. Keita and Maximo Adams , who combined for 17 rebounds against Wyoming, set the blueprint in the second half for what a serviceable frontcourt — and rebounding unit — can look like. But as Malone alluded to after his third win as a college coach, it has to be a five-man effort in crashing the glass, one the Tar Heels will need for 40 minutes on Friday. 
 Dating back to the preseason, UNC hasn’t solved microwave scorers particularly well — allowing an opposing player to eclipse 22 points in every game but two (three exhibition, three regular season). The Bulldogs certainly have the personnel to continue that trend, but Keita’s six-block, three-steal effort alleviated perimeter-to-rim stress on defenders, a promising recipe that kept Wyoming’s leading scorer, Nasir Meyer, at 17 points on 21 shots. 
 Georgia’s frontcourt limitations, surrendering 88 points in the paint through three games, present another opportunity for Terrence Brown to get downhill and for North Carolina to attack the rim. After a barrage of 3-pointers against Western Carolina, the Tar Heels have prioritized layups and dunks since, creating another offensive layer for Malone’s squad, which also lacks a dominant inside game. 
 Last Meeting: UNC is 13-5 all-time against Georgia, with the most recent installment coming on Nov. 18, 1998. The Tar Heels are 8-0 at home in the series.
